purpose: silver_flights holds one row per scheduled commercial flight departing the New York-area airports EWR, JFK, and LGA across the first half of 2013, combining schedule, actual-time, delay, aircraft, and airport reference attributes.
usage: Read the table at the grain of one row per flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number combination. Consumers must handle nulls in the actual-time and delay columns (dep_hhmm, dep_delay_minutes, arr_hhmm, arr_delay_minutes, air_time_minutes) for cancelled or unrecorded flights, in tail_number when unmatched, in the aircraft_* columns when the registry lookup has no match, and in the dest_* reference columns when the destination airport lookup has no match.
limitations: The profile confirms whole-row distinctness (duplicate_row_rate 0.0) but not that flight_date/carrier_code/flight_number is the true grain; a deterministic grain measurement must confirm it before reliance. Aircraft and destination-reference columns carry sparse, correlated nulls from lookup gaps rather than data quality defects. captured_at is a pipeline ingestion timestamp spanning a 15-second window, not flight-domain data, and is retained because the profile enumerates every column.
